definitions.explanation: The exit or entrance on the north side of a building, typically a train station. Japanese stations commonly label exits by compass direction.

examples.japanese: {北口|きたぐち}で{待|ま}っています。
examples.english: I'll be waiting at the north exit.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{北口|きたぐち}を{出|で}て{右|みぎ}に{曲|ま}がってください。
examples.english: Go out the north exit of the station and turn right.

examples.japanese: {北口|きたぐち}の{前|まえ}にバス{停|てい}があります。
examples.english: There is a bus stop in front of the north exit.

notes:
{北口|きたぐち} means the north exit or entrance, most commonly of a train station. Japanese stations typically label exits by compass direction to help people navigate.

FORMS:
{北|きた} (north) + {口|ぐち} (exit/entrance, with rendaku from くち)

STATION EXIT SET:
- {北口|きたぐち}: north exit
- {南口|みなみぐち}: south exit
- {東口|ひがしぐち}: east exit
- {西口|にしぐち}: west exit

OTHER ～{口|ぐち} COMPOUNDS:
- {改札口|かいさつぐち}: ticket gate
- {出口|でぐち}: exit
- {入口|いりぐち}: entrance
- {中央口|ちゅうおうぐち}: central exit

USAGE:
Very common when giving directions to meet someone, especially at stations: 「{北口|きたぐち}で{待|ま}ってて」 (Wait at the north exit). The area around each exit often has a distinct character — different shops, bus routes, and landmarks.
